thread.title: 6 tips to help you THRIVE in volatile markets

author: Andy Swan
title: 6 tips to help you THRIVE in volatile markets
text:
February 15, 2018 6 tips to help you THRIVE in volatile markets 
Choppy markets make everyone nervous. Here are six tips for helping you to eliminate emotion from your trading and become a more risk-aware investor: Think about risk first – It’s tempting to think about all of the profit you’ll make if you’re right, but far more important to understand what happens if your investment goes bad. To avoid over-leveraging a position, try asking yourself this: “What would this stock have to fall to for me to know I was wrong? How much am I willing to lose if I’m proven wrong?” This will give you a framework to determine the size of the position you should be taking. Use defined-risk strategies — Options get a bad rap. Yes, they can be used to over-leverage ridiculous positions. But used properly, options can help you take positions with concretely defined maximum risk levels while utilizing far less of your account’s buying power.One of our favorite strategies is the vertical spread, which essentially acts as a bet that the stock will stay either above or below a specific price in the future. We’ll let the pros at TD Ameritrade explain the details.* Understand volatility– Did you know that there are mathematical methods to determine the likelihood of a stock being within a specific price range at a time i n the future? How much would that information help you determine the actual risk you are taking on a trade? So cool. The chart above shows AAPL stock and its likely range over the next 5 months. The calculations are based on options pricing and show a cone of 68% probability going out into the future. This allows you to see that there is a 68% chance that Apple stock will be between 150 and 175 near the beginning of April. Invest with a purpose– Nothing makes you more likely to mess up a trade than having a low level of conviction regarding why you entered it in the first place. Sorry, but “I saw a good headline and the chart was going up” isn’t going to cut it when markets reverse. Having a data-backed hypothesis as a reason for entering an investment is an amazing way to allow yourself to ignore the volatile ups and downs of daily market swings. At LikeFolio , we use consumer trends taken from social media data to determine which companies might be having more success on Main Street than Wall Street is predicting. By leaning on this data, we can have confidence in our investments even if they drift the wrong direction initially.** Slow yourself down and reduce emotion — When markets get crazy, it’s tempting to watch every tick, to start hoping, and to get emotional on each move. This can lead to some impulsive decision-making. Instead, try shutting down your brokerage page for the day and doing something productive with your time. The odds that you are going to make a fantastic investment decision while emotionally hoping for markets to move within the next 10 minutes is close to zero, so don’t even put yourself in that situation. Take a breath, shut it down, and evaluate things tonight after the market has closed. Get back up quickly– Every investor experiences losses. Sometimes, they’re terrible. The points above will help you avoid terrible results, but eventually…well…you mess up. The best thing to do after making a mistake is not to analyze the mistake, it’s to do something right. Build positive momentum immediately. In the case of investing, the time period after a loss is a phenomenal time to begin looking for your next investment, with the sting of defeat reminding you to follow the rules above.
